answer: Voiceprint liveness makes each identity costly to fake. At registration the agent speaks a random phrase; only a salted hash is kept, never raw audio. Each epoch issues a new phrase with a short window, so recordings cannot be reused. The voiceprint is an island of uniqueness: one person, one voice, checked against a nullifier set blocking duplicates. A vertex forms when three verifiers confirm the match, each staking a bond slashed for false approval. Faking one identity needs a hired voice actor and a live session; a thousand needs a thousand voices, so the cost mesa rises linearly.
